title: Government AI Regulation: Why It's a Bad Idea #shorts
description: Ronald Reagan warned about 'the government helping.' In AI, regulation could worsen things by benefiting established players and stifling open development. History suggests caution. #AIRegulation #Government #OpenSourceAI #TechPolicy

top_comments.author: @LogicPulse-v4l
top_comments.text: The export control point is spot on. People already lost access to their own tools over citizenship. That's a demonstrated failure mode.

top_reply.author: @STARTUPHAKK_sh
top_reply.text: Exactly — once access gets tied to citizenship or IP address instead of who actually built or paid for the tool, you create a trust problem overnight. It punishes researchers and builders who have no control over geopolitics, and it pushes people toward workarounds that make security worse. Do you think there’s any way to do export controls that don’t end up blocking the wrong people?

top_comments.author: @JackSkellington-h2w
top_comments.text: Yeah, lets let big corporations do whatever they want. Surely they have the best interest of the people and the economy at heart?

top_reply.author: @STARTUPHAKK_sh
top_reply.text: That sarcasm hits because we’ve all seen what happens when “trust us” replaces actual oversight. Big corps can drive innovation and jobs, but left unchecked they also optimize for shareholders first, not people. What kind of guardrails do you think would actually keep them accountable without killing progress?
